page.overview:
Who is Rómendacil II?

Rómendacil II was the son of King Calmacil, and the elder brother of Calimehtar. He was originally named Minalcar.

Minalcar was born in TA 1126, toward the end of the long reign of Hyarmendacil I and he rose to power early because his uncle Narmacil I (eldest son of Atanatar II) wished to devote himself to a life of pleasure.

He was "Regent of the realm" of Gondor from TA 1240 and struck a decisive blow against the Easterlings, whom he heavily defeated in TA 1248 near the Sea of Rhûn. He also fortified Gondor and made pacts with the Northmen of Rhovanion, all before he took the throne. After Narmacil's death, he remained Regent for ten years under his father Calmacil.

When he finally ascended to the throne after the death of his father, he immediately took the name Rómendacil (East-victor), as his distant forefather Tarostar had done. He was responsible for the Argonath, the pillars of the Kings. They stood above Nen Hithoel on the Anduin river long into the Fourth Age and appear prominently in .
